episodes.179760: A stationary front located from southeastern Montana to northwestern North Dakota was a focus mechanism for some nocturnal thunderstorms.
episodes.179766: A stacked upper level low pressure system drifted from the Ohio River Valley to eastern Kentucky during the early morning hours of the 20th. South-southeasterly windflow around the low was efficient in transporting deep moisture into the area from the coastal Carolinas, allowing precipitable water values to rise into the 1.5 to 1.7 inch range along the crest of the Blue Ridge in Virginia south of Roanoke. Winds were nearly unidirectional with height around the low, with speeds varying between 15kt and 25kt between 925mb and 500mb per Storm Prediction Center Mesoscale Analysis.  Most-Unstable CAPEs along the Blue Ridge varied between 500 and 750 J/Kg through the night, but increased to around 1,000 J/Kg at around 5 AM/09 UTC as a wave of energy passed across the area. Multiple bands of training cells developed along the Blue Ridge.
episodes.179782: Mid-level Pacific moisture wrapping around a strong area of high pressure over northern Mexico resulted in some virga showers and dry thunderstorms over central and eastern New Mexico. One of these dry thunderstorms produced a dry microburst at Cannon AFB.
episodes.180095: Mesoscale convective complex responsible for strong marine wind gust across Nature Coast and waterspout offshore Pinellas County.
episodes.180096: Thunderstorms with MCS over northern peninsula produce gusty marine winds over Nature Coast and West Central Florida waters.
episodes.180110: An upper level low was located over northern GA with shortwave energy rotating through the base of the trough. Moderate instability and a moist air mass was present with precipitable water values around 1.8 inches. Slow moving thunderstorms with high rain rates moved over the Augusta metro area.
episodes.180158: Thunderstorms developed along a cold front during the afternoon on June 20th, in a hot environment with mid-90s temperatures. These storms produced wind gusts above 60 mph, hail up to quarter sized, as well as heavy rainfall into the evening.
episodes.180180: Thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong to severe winds along the coast south of Cape Canaveral.
episodes.180181: Severe storms pushing offshore produced wind damage and severe hail and gusts in Brevard County.
episodes.180182: Gusty showers and storms produced strong wind gusts along the coast.
episodes.180285: For a second consecutive day, showers and thunderstorms across eastern Nevada caused gusty outflow winds.
episodes.180291: Thunderstorms with a MCS over the northern peninsula produce heavy rain and flooding near Williston in Levy County.
episodes.181009: Thunderstorms initially formed over Montana in the vicinity of a surface low that gradually lifted northward near the North Dakota and Montana border. The first storms moved into southwest North Dakota, with one becoming severe producing one-inch diameter hail to the southeast of Golva in Golden Valley County. Late that night, additional thunderstorms developed over northwest North Dakota as a low level jet increased over the area. Another storm became severe, producing wind gusts of 77 mph near Ray in Williams County.
episodes.181013: A surface boundary set up over central North Dakota, as a weak shortwave trough approached the region. Very strong instability developed through central North Dakota, with elevated deep-layer shear. Initial severe storms produced large hail, with a mix of large hail and damaging wind gusts as time went on. Some of the winds became very damaging over north-central North Dakota. Near Balta, a farm sustained heavy property and tree damage with a measured wind gust of 110 mph, with other farms in the area suffering mainly tree damage. Tree damage also was reported in Rugby. Further north, in Rolette County, the city of Dunseith was severely affected with many trees snapped or uprooted, along with downed power lines. One individual was injured (indirect) when he was burned while cleaning up tree branches and came in contact with a live downed electrical wire. Near the City of Rolette, a porch and multiple teepees were damaged. This damage was attributed to a gustnado, which formed out  ahead of the thunderstorm. Video evidence showed there was no connection from the ground circulation to the cloud base, and based on that, it was determined that this was a gustnado and not a tornado. NWS policy directives dictate that a gustnado is classified as a Thunderstorm Wind event in StormData.
episodes.181031: Two distinct short-wave troughs embedded within an upper-level trough west of the region brought 2 rounds of strong to severe storms across the local area under active SW flow. The first round of storms moved inland across the Suwannee River Valley in the morning and tracked eastward across the area through early afternoon. The next round of storm occurred during the evening toward the Atlantic coast. Widespread wind gusts of 40-50 mph and small hail occurred with many of the strong storms with large hail from severe storms and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.181095: A few thunderstorms across far southeast Montana resulted in mainly some strong and damaging winds.
episodes.181097: An isolated thunderstorm damaged some vehicles and buildings.
episodes.181182: The middle part of June was unusually stormy across the area.  Numerous rounds of strong to severe storms impacted the region with multiple squall lines producing strong to severe winds across the coastal waters.
episodes.181204: An upper-level trough west of the region focused a series of short-wave troughs across the local area. The upper-level forcing combined with high moisture combined with a low level 850 mb jet of 35 kts enhanced morning convection across NE FL. Isolated strong to severe storms expanded north and east across NE FL and SE GA into the afternoon and evening.
episodes.181214: An upper-level trough west of the region focused a series of short-wave troughs across the local area. The upper-level forcing combined with high moisture combined with a low level 850 mb jet of 35 kts enhanced morning convection across NE FL. Isolated strong to severe storms expanded north and east across NE FL and SE GA into the afternoon and evening.
episodes.182365: Upper level disturbances moved across the region on the periphery of a ridge aloft. This produced multiple days of stormy weather with some storms becoming severe.
episodes.182406: A northwest upper level flow regime was in place. This setup commonly supports summertime severe thunderstorms. This event was one of those days where very steep lapse rates and high shear values supported several severe thunderstorms with severe marine wind.
episodes.182407: A northwest upper level flow regime was in place. This setup commonly supports summertime severe thunderstorms. This event was one of those days where very steep lapse rates and high shear values supported several severe thunderstorms with damaging wind and large hail.
episodes.182408: A northwest upper level flow regime was in place. This setup commonly supports summertime severe thunderstorms. This event was one of those days where very steep lapse rates and high shear values supported several severe thunderstorms with damaging wind, flash flooding, hail and one EF-2 tornado.
episodes.182521: Severe thunderstorms developed in a very moist and unstable airmass across the Concho Valley and Heartland. The severe storms produced large hail and damaging winds including significant wind damage around Christoval due to a microburst.
episodes.182558: Low pressure and modestly unstable conditions lingering across the region in wake of shortwave energy shifting offshore led to thunderstorms capable of producing strong wind gusts.
episodes.182614: A combination of heavy rain and mountain snow melt brought minor flooding along the Wind River. The flooding remained in the low lying areas near the river and caused no property damage or road closure.
episodes.182888: Low pressure over the SE U.S. provided a south to southwest wind flow across South Florida. This helped to focus strong showers and thunderstorms from Lake Okeechobee to the SE coast of Florida during the afternoon hours.
episodes.183381: Waves of showers and thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a stalled frontal zone, and in the vicinity of the Blue Ridge escarpment in response to upslope flow. The result was localized areas of heavy-to-excessive rainfall, with anywhere from 5 to 10 inches reported over a 24-36 hour period. Isolated flash flooding developed across portions of the foothills and the Piedmont.

Flash flooding occurred within the Ocala city limits from about 5-6 inches of rainfall during the morning hours during about a 3 hour accumulation period. The first flash flood report to the NWS was at 9:42 am when Marion county dispatch reported that 3 lanes of traffic were closed on Southeast 17th Street near Southeast Lake Weir Avenue. At 10:15 am, a local newspaper reported that East Silver Springs Blvd, west of South Pine Avenue, was flooding with some portions of the road closed due to flood water. At 10:34 am, the public reported a car was stuck in flood water under bridge on U.S. Highway 441 south of Southeast 3rd Avenue. Around 3 to 4 inches of rainfall was measured in this area around the time of this report since about 8 am. Police and emergency vehicles were on scene. On 6/21 around 9:32 am, law enforcement reported that County Road 475A (SW 27th Avenue) in Ocala was closed due to flood water from SW 66th Street to SW 42nd Street.
Minor flooding occurred along the Wind River near Riverton. The flooding remained in low lying areas near the river and caused no damage.

Emergency manager reported flash flooding developed in southwest Rowan County after 4 to 5 inches fell in just a few hours. The most significant flooding was in the city of Kannapolis. A small stream inundated Mable Ave and Marie Ave near the Cabarrus County line. A tributary og Irish Buffalo Creek overflowed onto Pump Station Rd. Another stream overflowed onto West 22nd St. Farther northwest, East Fork flooded a road at the Iredell County line, while Jackson Rd and Highway 150 were inundated by Sills Creek.

Emergency manager reported flash flooding developed in the city of Kannapolis after 4 to 5 inches of rain fell in just a few hours. Irish Buffalo Creek overflowed its banks on the west side of the city and inundated Pine St and Tiffany Dr. Around thirty people were evacuated from multiple mobile homes in this area and several of the homes were inundated and damaged.

A thunderstorm developed a vigorous mesovortex along a boundary over Lake Salvador just before 2100 UTC. This mesovortex intensified and tracked northwest into the Salvador Wildlife Management Area where a large tornado damage path was visible on high resolution satellite imagery. Widespread tree damage including swaths of uproots and snaps of softwood trees as well as ground scouring and rowing marks from the parent mesovortex were observed indicative of a significant tornado. KLIX radar imagery supports this approximate 4 mile track inland with a 40 knot rotational velocity and weak tornado debris signature evident to at least 4000 feet where the most severe damage was located midway along the path. Thereafter, the tornado path gradually narrowed and weakened and its estimated the tornado dissipated around 21:07 UTC. A ground survey was later performed to assess the highest end damage from this tornado which confirmed the existence of several snapped bald cypress trees.
